mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically different from a pre-rate hike period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.3% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a faster than expected rate cut cycle, which drives a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite inflation above 0.3% for the required period (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) accompanied by a decline in UNRATE (labor supply) creates a labor market tightness signal that predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while UNRATE decreases by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day IC < 0.05 and forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (goods demand) of at least 3% for two consecutive quarters is interpreted as a demand shock that supports equity valuations, producing a positive 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines by >=3% in a month and persists for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: IC for this signal vs. baseline is < 0.01 over 60 days (p > 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls by more than 5% in two consecutive months, it indicates supply-side weakness that reduces growth expectations and drives a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >5% in a month and repeats the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in HOUST (housing starts) and PAYEMS (employment) above their 12-month moving averages signals a dual labor market recovery that increases investor confidence and drives a positive 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA and PAYEMS > 12-month MA in the same month

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS (money supply growth) below -2% for three consecutive months indicates a deflationary bias that raises discount rates and predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below -2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 6% and FEDFUNDS rises above 1% simultaneously, the combination signals a shift to a more restrictive policy regime that is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
